**Commentary on Surat al-Saff**

It is a Madinan surah.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, and (another chain) from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "We discussed among ourselves: Which of you will go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him, 'Which deeds are most beloved to Allah?' None of us stood up. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man to us, and he gathered us and recited to us this surah, meaning the whole of Surat al-Saff." Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it.[[Musnad (5/452).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid al-Bayruti [[In manuscript A: "al-Sarwari".]] related to us by reading, saying: My father informed me, I heard al-Awza'i, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to me, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman related to me, Abdullah ibn Salam related to me: that some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If we were to send someone to the Messenger of Allah to ask him about the deeds most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" But none of us went to him, and we were too shy to ask him about that. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then called those men one by one until he had gathered them, and this surah was revealed concerning them: "Glorified is what is in the heavens..." (Surat al-Saff). Abdullah ibn Salam said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to us in full. Abu Salamah said: Abdullah ibn Salam recited it to us in full. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said: Abu Salamah recited it to us in full. Al-Awza'i said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir recited it to us in full. My father said: al-Awza'i recited it to us in full.

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "We sat with a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and discussed, and we said: 'If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, we would do them.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [[Its text here adds in brackets: "Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do."]]" Abdullah ibn Salam said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to us. Abu Salamah said: Ibn Salam recited it to us. Yahya said: Abu Salamah recited it to us. Ibn Kathir said: al-Awza'i recited it to us. Abdullah said: Ibn Kathir recited it to us.

Then al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Kathir has been contradicted in the chain of this hadith from al-Awza'i. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn Salam, or: from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3309).]]

I say: Imam Ahmad also narrated it in this way, from Ya'mur, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with the same chain.[[Musnad (5/452).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: al-Walid ibn Muslim also narrated this hadith from al-Awza'i, similar to the narration of Muhammad ibn Kathir.

I say: al-Walid ibn Yazid also narrated it from al-Awza'i, as Ibn Kathir narrated it.

I say: This hadith was related to me by the scholar and narrator (musnid) Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abi Talib al-Hajjar, by reading to him while I listened: Abu al-Muna Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Lati [[In manuscript A: "al-Laythi".]] informed us; Abu al-Waqt Abd al-Awwal ibn Isa ibn Shu'ayb al-Sijzi informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Dawudi informed us; Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawiyyah al-Sarakhsi informed us; Isa ibn Umar ibn Imran al-Samarqandi informed us; the Imam and memorizer (hafiz) Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi informed us with his entire Musnad: Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, from al-Awza'i... and he mentioned its chain and text similarly. The recitation of this surah was transmitted to us in a chain going back to our shaykh Abu al-Abbas al-Hajjar; however, he did not recite it himself, because he was unlettered (ummi), and time was too short to teach it to him. But the great memorizer Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Dhahabi, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me: al-Qadi Taqi al-Din Sulayman ibn al-Shaykh Abi Umar informed us; Abu al-Muna ibn al-Lati informed us, and he mentioned it with its chain. It was transmitted to me by one route, and he recited it to me in full. All praise and grace belong to Allah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

The discussion of His words, ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, has already passed more than once, sufficient to dispense with repeating it.

* *

His words, ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ are a rebuke against one who makes a promise or says a thing he does not fulfil. For this reason, some of the scholars of the early generations (salaf) used this noble verse as evidence that fulfilling a promise is obligatory in all cases, whether or not it results in a loss for the person to whom it was made. They also cited from the Sunnah what is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (33), and Sahih Muslim, no. (59), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] In another hadith in the Sahih: "Whoever has four qualities is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a characteristic of hypocrisy until he gives it up," and he mentioned among them breaking a promise.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (34), and Sahih Muslim, no. (58), from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] We have fully discussed these two hadiths at the beginning of our commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari (Sharh al-Bukhari), and all praise and grace belong to Allah. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, emphasized this rebuke against them with His words: ﴿Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.﴾

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'ah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us [in our house] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] while I was a child. I went out to play, and my mother said: "Abdullah, come, I will give you something." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "What did you intend to give him?" She said: "Dates." He said: "As for you, if you had not done so, a lie would have been recorded against you."[[Musnad (3/447) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4991).]]

Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, held that if a promise is linked to a material consideration (ghurm) payable to the one promised, then fulfilling it is obligatory, as if someone said to another: "Marry, and I will give you such-and-such every day." If he marries, he is obliged to give it to him for as long as that continues, because the right of a human being is attached to it, and it is based on strictness (mudayiqah). The majority of scholars held that it is not obligatory in every case. They interpreted the verse as having been revealed when they wished that jihad would be prescribed for them; then when it was prescribed, some of them shrank from it, like His words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear Allah or with even greater fear, and they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You would delay us for a short term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even as much as a thread." Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built up high﴾ [An-Nisa': 77–78]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been revealed?" But when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting before death﴾ [Muhammad: 20], and so on. This verse has the same meaning. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ He said: Some of the believers, before jihad was prescribed, used to say: "We wish that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, would guide us to the deed most beloved to Him, so that we might do it." So Allah informed His Prophet that the deed most beloved to Him is faith in Him without doubt, and striving against the people of His disobedience who opposed faith and did not acknowledge it. When fighting was prescribed, some of the believers disliked it and found its command hard, so Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/56).]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The believers said: "If we knew the deed most beloved to Allah, we would do it." So Allah guided them to the deed most beloved to Him, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a structure joined firmly﴾, thus making it clear to them. Then they were tested with it on the day of Uhud, and they turned their backs and fled from the Prophet ﷺ. So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ And He said: "The most beloved of you to Me is the one who fights in My cause."

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning fighting, where a man says, "I fought," when he did not fight; "I stabbed," when he did not stab; "I struck," when he did not strike; "I endured," when he did not endure.[[In manuscript M: "I did not fight."]]

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: It was revealed as a rebuke to a people who used to say, "We killed, we struck, we stabbed, and we did," when they had not done so.

Ibn Yazid said: It was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who used to promise victory to the Muslims and did not fulfil that to them.

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾, that he said: It refers to jihad.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ up to His words ﴿as if they were a structure joined firmly﴾, that what lies between these is about a group of the Ansar, among them Abdullah ibn Rawahah. They said in a gathering: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them until we die." So Allah revealed this concerning them. Then Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: "I will not cease to be a detained one in the cause of Allah until I die." Then he was killed as a martyr.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' related to us, Ali ibn Mushir [[In manuscript A: "Shihr".]] related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad al-Duwali [[In manuscript A: "al-Daylami".]], from his father, who said: Abu Musa sent for the reciters of the people of Basrah, and three hundred men came to him, all of whom had memorized the Qur'an. He said: "You are the reciters of the people of Basrah and their best." And he said: "We used to recite a surah that we likened to one of the Musabbihat, but it was made to slip from us, except that I have retained from it: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? A testimony will be written upon your necks, and you will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection﴾."

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a structure joined firmly﴾. This is information from Him, the Exalted, about His love for His believing servants when they stand in rows, facing the enemies of Allah in the fierceness of battle, fighting in the cause of Allah against those who disbelieve in Allah, so that the word of Allah may be supreme, and His religion may be the manifest and dominant one above all other religions.

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Mujalid said: Abu al-Wadday informed us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three (groups) Allah laughs at (with pleasure): a man who rises during the night (for prayer), a people when they line up for prayer, and a people when they line up for battle."

Ibn Majah also narrated it through the hadith of Mujalid, from Abu al-Wadday Jabr ibn Nawf, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (3/80) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (200). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/87): "This chain contains weakness. Mujalid ibn Sa'id, although Muslim included him in his Sahih, narrated from him only in conjunction with others. Ibn 'Adi said: most of what he narrates is not preserved."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, al-Aswad (i.e., Ibn Shaybān) narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir narrated to me, who said: Mutarrif said: "A hadith had reached me from Abu Dharr, and I longed to meet him. So I met him and said: 'O Abu Dharr, a hadith had reached me from you, and I longed to meet you.' He said: 'May your father be blessed! You have met (me), so speak.' I said: 'It reached me that you claim the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told you that Allah loves three and hates three?' He said: 'Indeed. For I do not think I would lie against my beloved (ﷺ).' I said: 'Who are these three whom Allah loves?' He said: 'A man who fought in the way of Allah, who went out seeking reward and striving, then met the enemy and was killed; and you find it in the Book of Allah, the Revealed Book,' then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure.﴾ And he mentioned the hadith."

Thus he narrated this hadith by this route, with this context and this wording, and abridged it. At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Ribʿi ibn Hirash, from Zayd ibn Zabyan, from Abu Dharr, in a fuller and more complete form than this context. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2568), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/84, 3/207). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sahih hadith."]] We have cited it in another place, and to Allah belongs all praise.

And from Ka'b al-Ahbar that he said: Allah the Exalted says to Muhammad (ﷺ): "My servant, the one who relies (upon Me), the chosen one. He is neither harsh nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives. His birthplace is Makkah, his migration is to Taybah, and his kingdom is in al-Sham. His community are the ones who praise (Allah), praising Allah in every state and every station. For them is a humming like the humming of bees in the open sky at dawn. They wash their extremities and tie their waistwraps at their midsections. Their row in battle is like their row in prayer." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure.﴾ "They are the shepherds of the sun, who pray the prayer wherever it reaches them, even upon the back of a beast." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row﴾: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not fight the enemy unless they lined up against them, and this is an instruction from Allah to the believers. He said: And His words ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾ means joined together, one part to another, from lining up in battle.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Joined one part to another."

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾ means firm, not moving, joined one part to another.

Qatadah said: ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾: Have you not seen the owner of a building, how he does not like his building to be uneven? Likewise, Allah the Mighty and Majestic [loves that] [[Addition from manuscripts M and A.]] His command not be uneven. Indeed Allah has arranged the believers in their fighting and arranged them in their prayer, so hold to the command of Allah, for it is a protection for whoever holds to it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated all of this.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, from Abu Bahriyyah [[In A: "from Abu Yahya."]], who said: They used to dislike fighting on horseback and preferred fighting on foot, due to the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure﴾. He said: Abu Bahriyyah used to say: "If you see me turn my head in the row, then strike my jaw." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/57).]]

They said in a gathering: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them until we die." So Allah revealed this concerning them. Then Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: "I will not cease to be a detained one in the cause of Allah until I die." Then he was killed as a martyr.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' related to us, Ali ibn Mushir [[In manuscript A: "Shihr".]] related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad al-Duwali [[In manuscript A: "al-Daylami".]], from his father, who said: Abu Musa sent for the reciters of the people of Basrah, and three hundred men came to him, all of whom had memorized the Qur'an. **Commentary on Surat al-Saff**

It is a Madinan surah.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, and (another chain) from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "We discussed among ourselves: Which of you will go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask him, 'Which deeds are most beloved to Allah?' None of us stood up. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man to us, and he gathered us and recited to us this surah, meaning the whole of Surat al-Saff." Thus Imam Ahmad narrated it.[[Musnad (5/452).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid al-Bayruti [[In manuscript A: "al-Sarwari".]] related to us by reading, saying: My father informed me, I heard al-Awza'i, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir related to me, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman related to me, Abdullah ibn Salam related to me: that some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If we were to send someone to the Messenger of Allah to ask him about the deeds most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?" But none of us went to him, and we were too shy to ask him about that. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then called those men one by one until he had gathered them, and this surah was revealed concerning them: "Glorified is what is in the heavens..." (Surat al-Saff). Abdullah ibn Salam said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to us in full. Abu Salamah said: Abdullah ibn Salam recited it to us in full. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir said: Abu Salamah recited it to us in full. Al-Awza'i said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir recited it to us in full. My father said: al-Awza'i recited it to us in full.

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: "We sat with a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and discussed, and we said: 'If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, we would do them.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [[Its text here adds in brackets: "Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do."]]" Abdullah ibn Salam said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to us. Abu Salamah said: Ibn Salam recited it to us. Yahya said: Abu Salamah recited it to us. Ibn Kathir said: al-Awza'i recited it to us. Abdullah said: Ibn Kathir recited it to us.

Then al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Kathir has been contradicted in the chain of this hadith from al-Awza'i. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn Salam, or: from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3309).]]

I say: Imam Ahmad also narrated it in this way, from Ya'mur, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with the same chain.[[Musnad (5/452).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: al-Walid ibn Muslim also narrated this hadith from al-Awza'i, similar to the narration of Muhammad ibn Kathir.

I say: al-Walid ibn Yazid also narrated it from al-Awza'i, as Ibn Kathir narrated it.

I say: This hadith was related to me by the scholar and narrator (musnid) Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abi Talib al-Hajjar, by reading to him while I listened: Abu al-Muna Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Lati [[In manuscript A: "al-Laythi".]] informed us; Abu al-Waqt Abd al-Awwal ibn Isa ibn Shu'ayb al-Sijzi informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Dawudi informed us; Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawiyyah al-Sarakhsi informed us; Isa ibn Umar ibn Imran al-Samarqandi informed us; the Imam and memorizer (hafiz) Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi informed us with his entire Musnad: Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, from al-Awza'i... and he mentioned its chain and text similarly. The recitation of this surah was transmitted to us in a chain going back to our shaykh Abu al-Abbas al-Hajjar; however, he did not recite it himself, because he was unlettered (ummi), and time was too short to teach it to him. But the great memorizer Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Dhahabi, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me: al-Qadi Taqi al-Din Sulayman ibn al-Shaykh Abi Umar informed us; Abu al-Muna ibn al-Lati informed us, and he mentioned it with its chain. It was transmitted to me by one route, and he recited it to me in full. All praise and grace belong to Allah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

The discussion of His words, ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, has already passed more than once, sufficient to dispense with repeating it.

His words, ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ are a rebuke against one who makes a promise or says a thing he does not fulfil. For this reason, some of the scholars of the early generations (salaf) used this noble verse as evidence that fulfilling a promise is obligatory in all cases, whether or not it results in a loss for the person to whom it was made. They also cited from the Sunnah what is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, emphasized this rebuke against them with His words: ﴿Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.﴾

I went out to play, and my mother said: "Abdullah, come, I will give you something." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "What did you intend to give him?" She said: "Dates." If he marries, he is obliged to give it to him for as long as that continues, because the right of a human being is attached to it, and it is based on strictness (mudayiqah). The majority of scholars held that it is not obligatory in every case. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn Salam, or: from Abu Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Salam.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3309).]]

I say: Imam Ahmad also narrated it in this way, from Ya'mur, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with the same chain.[[Musnad (5/452).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: al-Walid ibn Muslim also narrated this hadith from al-Awza'i, similar to the narration of Muhammad ibn Kathir.

I say: al-Walid ibn Yazid also narrated it from al-Awza'i, as Ibn Kathir narrated it.

I say: This hadith was related to me by the scholar and narrator (musnid) Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abi Talib al-Hajjar, by reading to him while I listened: Abu al-Muna Abdullah ibn Umar ibn al-Lati [[In manuscript A: "al-Laythi".]] informed us; Abu al-Waqt Abd al-Awwal ibn Isa ibn Shu'ayb al-Sijzi informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Dawudi informed us; Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawiyyah al-Sarakhsi informed us; Isa ibn Umar ibn Imran al-Samarqandi informed us; the Imam and memorizer (hafiz) Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi informed us with his entire Musnad: Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, from al-Awza'i... and he mentioned its chain and text similarly. The recitation of this surah was transmitted to us in a chain going back to our shaykh Abu al-Abbas al-Hajjar; however, he did not recite it himself, because he was unlettered (ummi), and time was too short to teach it to him. But the great memorizer Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Dhahabi, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me: al-Qadi Taqi al-Din Sulayman ibn al-Shaykh Abi Umar informed us; Abu al-Muna ibn al-Lati informed us, and he mentioned it with its chain. It was transmitted to me by one route, and he recited it to me in full. All praise and grace belong to Allah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

The discussion of His words, ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, has already passed more than once, sufficient to dispense with repeating it.

* *

His words, ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ are a rebuke against one who makes a promise or says a thing he does not fulfil. For this reason, some of the scholars of the early generations (salaf) used this noble verse as evidence that fulfilling a promise is obligatory in all cases, whether or not it results in a loss for the person to whom it was made. They also cited from the Sunnah what is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is trusted he betrays."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (33), and Sahih Muslim, no. (59), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] In another hadith in the Sahih: "Whoever has four qualities is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a characteristic of hypocrisy until he gives it up," and he mentioned among them breaking a promise.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (34), and Sahih Muslim, no. (58), from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] We have fully discussed these two hadiths at the beginning of our commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari (Sharh al-Bukhari), and all praise and grace belong to Allah. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, emphasized this rebuke against them with His words: ﴿Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do.﴾

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'ah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us [in our house] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] while I was a child. I went out to play, and my mother said: "Abdullah, come, I will give you something." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "What did you intend to give him?" She said: "Dates." He said: "As for you, if you had not done so, a lie would have been recorded against you."[[Musnad (3/447) and Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (4991).]]

Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, held that if a promise is linked to a material consideration (ghurm) payable to the one promised, then fulfilling it is obligatory, as if someone said to another: "Marry, and I will give you such-and-such every day." If he marries, he is obliged to give it to him for as long as that continues, because the right of a human being is attached to it, and it is based on strictness (mudayiqah). The majority of scholars held that it is not obligatory in every case. They interpreted the verse as having been revealed when they wished that jihad would be prescribed for them; then when it was prescribed, some of them shrank from it, like His words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a party of them fear men as they should fear Allah or with even greater fear, and they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You would delay us for a short term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even as much as a thread." Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built up high﴾ [An-Nisa': 77–78]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been revealed?" But when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the look of one fainting before death﴾ [Muhammad: 20], and so on. This verse has the same meaning. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ He said: Some of the believers, before jihad was prescribed, used to say: "We wish that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, would guide us to the deed most beloved to Him, so that we might do it." So Allah informed His Prophet that the deed most beloved to Him is faith in Him without doubt, and striving against the people of His disobedience who opposed faith and did not acknowledge it. When fighting was prescribed, some of the believers disliked it and found its command hard, so Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/56).]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The believers said: "If we knew the deed most beloved to Allah, we would do it." So Allah guided them to the deed most beloved to Him, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a structure joined firmly﴾, thus making it clear to them. Then they were tested with it on the day of Uhud, and they turned their backs and fled from the Prophet ﷺ. So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ And He said: "The most beloved of you to Me is the one who fights in My cause."

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning fighting, where a man says, "I fought," when he did not fight; "I stabbed," when he did not stab; "I struck," when he did not strike; "I endured," when he did not endure.[[In manuscript M: "I did not fight."]]

Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: It was revealed as a rebuke to a people who used to say, "We killed, we struck, we stabbed, and we did," when they had not done so.

Ibn Yazid said: It was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who used to promise victory to the Muslims and did not fulfil that to them.

Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾, that he said: It refers to jihad.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ up to His words ﴿as if they were a structure joined firmly﴾, that what lies between these is about a group of the Ansar, among them Abdullah ibn Rawahah. They said in a gathering: "If we knew which deeds are most beloved to Allah, we would do them until we die." So Allah revealed this concerning them. Then Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: "I will not cease to be a detained one in the cause of Allah until I die." Then he was killed as a martyr.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' related to us, Ali ibn Mushir [[In manuscript A: "Shihr".]] related to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Harb ibn Abi al-Aswad al-Duwali [[In manuscript A: "al-Daylami".]], from his father, who said: Abu Musa sent for the reciters of the people of Basrah, and three hundred men came to him, all of whom had memorized the Qur'an. He said: "You are the reciters of the people of Basrah and their best." And he said: "We used to recite a surah that we likened to one of the Musabbihat, but it was made to slip from us, except that I have retained from it: ﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? A testimony will be written upon your necks, and you will be questioned about it on the Day of Resurrection﴾."

For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a structure joined firmly﴾. This is information from Him, the Exalted, about His love for His believing servants when they stand in rows, facing the enemies of Allah in the fierceness of battle, fighting in the cause of Allah against those who disbelieve in Allah, so that the word of Allah may be supreme, and His religion may be the manifest and dominant one above all other religions.

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Mujalid said: Abu al-Wadday informed us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three (groups) Allah laughs at (with pleasure): a man who rises during the night (for prayer), a people when they line up for prayer, and a people when they line up for battle."

Ibn Majah also narrated it through the hadith of Mujalid, from Abu al-Wadday Jabr ibn Nawf, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (3/80) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (200). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/87): "This chain contains weakness. Mujalid ibn Sa'id, although Muslim included him in his Sahih, narrated from him only in conjunction with others. Ibn 'Adi said: most of what he narrates is not preserved."]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, al-Aswad (i.e., Ibn Shaybān) narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir narrated to me, who said: Mutarrif said: "A hadith had reached me from Abu Dharr, and I longed to meet him. So I met him and said: 'O Abu Dharr, a hadith had reached me from you, and I longed to meet you.' He said: 'May your father be blessed! You have met (me), so speak.' I said: 'It reached me that you claim the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told you that Allah loves three and hates three?' He said: 'Indeed. For I do not think I would lie against my beloved (ﷺ).' I said: 'Who are these three whom Allah loves?' He said: 'A man who fought in the way of Allah, who went out seeking reward and striving, then met the enemy and was killed; and you find it in the Book of Allah, the Revealed Book,' then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure.﴾ And he mentioned the hadith."

Thus he narrated this hadith by this route, with this context and this wording, and abridged it. At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Ribʿi ibn Hirash, from Zayd ibn Zabyan, from Abu Dharr, in a fuller and more complete form than this context. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2568), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (5/84, 3/207). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sahih hadith."]] We have cited it in another place, and to Allah belongs all praise.

And from Ka'b al-Ahbar that he said: Allah the Exalted says to Muhammad (ﷺ): "My servant, the one who relies (upon Me), the chosen one. He is neither harsh nor coarse, nor loud in the markets, and he does not repay evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives. His birthplace is Makkah, his migration is to Taybah, and his kingdom is in al-Sham. His community are the ones who praise (Allah), praising Allah in every state and every station. For them is a humming like the humming of bees in the open sky at dawn. They wash their extremities and tie their waistwraps at their midsections. Their row in battle is like their row in prayer." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure.﴾ "They are the shepherds of the sun, who pray the prayer wherever it reaches them, even upon the back of a beast." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row﴾: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not fight the enemy unless they lined up against them, and this is an instruction from Allah to the believers. He said: And His words ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾ means joined together, one part to another, from lining up in battle.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Joined one part to another."

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾ means firm, not moving, joined one part to another.

Qatadah said: ﴿as if they were a solid structure﴾: Have you not seen the owner of a building, how he does not like his building to be uneven? Likewise, Allah the Mighty and Majestic [loves that] [[Addition from manuscripts M and A.]] His command not be uneven. Indeed Allah has arranged the believers in their fighting and arranged them in their prayer, so hold to the command of Allah, for it is a protection for whoever holds to it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated all of this.

Ibn Jarir said: Sa'id ibn Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, from Abu Bahriyyah [[In A: "from Abu Yahya."]], who said: They used to dislike fighting on horseback and preferred fighting on foot, due to the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure﴾. He said: Abu Bahriyyah used to say: "If you see me turn my head in the row, then strike my jaw." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/57).]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 61, verses 5–6:

He, the Exalted, says, reporting about His servant, His messenger, and the one He spoke to directly, Musa (Moses) son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, that he said to his people: ﴿Why do you harm me, when you know that I am the Messenger of Allah to you?﴾ That is: why do you inflict harm upon me, when you know my truthfulness in what I have brought you of the message?

In this there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for what he suffered from the disbelievers among his people and others, and a command to him to be patient. For this reason, he (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on Musa; he was harmed with more than this, and he was patient."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3405, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1062, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]] In it there is also a prohibition for the believers from harming the Prophet (ﷺ) or causing him any harm, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69]

* *

His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ means: when they turned away from following the truth while knowing it, Allah turned their hearts away from guidance, and made them dwell in doubt, bewilderment, and abandonment, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [al-An'am: 110] And He says: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him, and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has turned to, and We will burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾ [an-Nisa': 115] For this reason, Allah the Exalted said in this verse: ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

His saying: ﴿And when 'Isa son of Maryam said: O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah, and giving good news of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad﴾. That is: the Torah has given good news of me, and I am the confirmation of what it reported about him, and I give good news of the one after me, who is the Prophet, the unlettered, the Arab, the Meccan, Ahmad. 'Isa, peace be upon him, was the seal of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and he stood among the leaders of the Children of Israel giving good news of Muhammad, who is Ahmad, the seal of the prophets and messengers, after whom there is no messenger and no prophethood.

How excellent is the hadith that al-Bukhari reported, in which he said:

"Ḥaddathana Abu al-Yaman, ḥaddathana Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser) through whom Allah erases disbelief, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-‘Aqib (the Last).'"

Muslim also reported it, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with similar wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4896, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2354.]]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ḥaddathana al-Mas'udi, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named for us some names of himself, some of which we memorized, and he said: "I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, al-Hashir, al-Muqaffi, Prophet of Mercy, of Repentance, and of the Great Battle."

Muslim reported it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with the same.[[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 492, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2355.]] Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Injil﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him and support him. He said: Do you affirm, and accept My covenant on that? They said: We affirm. He said: Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 81]

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah did not send any prophet without taking from him the covenant: "If Muhammad is sent while you are alive, you shall surely follow him," and He took from him that he should take the same covenant from his nation: "If Muhammad is sent while they are alive, they shall surely follow him and support him."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Ḥaddathani Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us about yourself." He said: "The supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa, and my mother saw when she was carrying me, as if a light came out of her, by which the palaces of Busra in the land of Sham were illuminated."[[Reported by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/600) through Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Ibn Ishaq with it, and he said: "Khalid ibn Ma'dan is among the best of the Successors; he accompanied Mu'adh ibn Jabal and those after him from the Companions. So when a hadith is traced to the Companions, its chain is sound even if they did not include it." I say: It has also been transmitted with a connected chain, as will come in the narration of Ahmad.]]

This is a good chain. It has supporting narrations from other routes. Imam Ahmad said: Ḥaddathana 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, ḥaddathana Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from Sa'id ibn Suwayd al-Kalbi, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal [in A: "Bilal"] al-Sulami, from al-'Irbad ibn Sariyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I am, with Allah, the Seal of the Prophets, and Adam was still kneaded in his clay. I will inform you of the first of that: the supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa about me, and the vision my mother saw. Likewise, the mothers of the prophets see visions."[[The Musnad (4/127). Sa'id ibn Suwayd was declared reliable only by Ibn Hibban.]]

Ahmad also said: Ḥaddathana Abu al-Nadr, ḥaddathana al-Faraj ibn Fadalah, ḥaddathana Luqman ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard Abu Umamah say: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, what was the beginning of your affair?" He said: "The supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa, and my mother saw that a light came out of her, by which the palaces of Sham were illuminated."[[The Musnad (5/262).]]

Ahmad also said: Ḥaddathana Hasan ibn Musa: I heard Khudayj, the brother of Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent us to the Negus, and we were about eighty men, among them 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Ja'far, 'Abdullah ibn [‘Urfutah]  [[Addition from the Musnad; there is a blank in the other manuscripts.]], 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, and Abu Musa. They came to the Negus, and Quraysh sent 'Amr ibn al-'As and 'Umarah ibn al-Walid with a gift. When the two entered upon the Negus, they prostrated to him, then they came at him from his right and his left, and said to him: "Some men from our cousin's people have settled in your land, and they have turned away from us and from our religion." He said: "Where are they?" They said: "They are in your land, so send for them." So he sent for them. Ja'far said: "I will be your speaker today." They followed him. He greeted and did not prostrate. They said to him: "Why do you not prostrate to the king?" He said: "We do not prostrate except to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "Indeed Allah sent His Messenger to us, and commanded us not to prostrate to anyone except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and commanded us with prayer and zakat."

'Amr ibn al-'As said: "Indeed they oppose you regarding 'Isa son of Maryam." He said: "What do you say about 'Isa son of Maryam and his mother?" They said: "We say as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: He is the Word of Allah and His Spirit, which He cast to the virgin chaste, whom no man has touched and no child has entered." He took a stick from the ground and said: "O assembly of Abyssinians, priests and monks, by Allah, they do not exceed what we say about him, not even this much. Welcome to you and to those who came from his presence. I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, and that he is the one we find in the Gospel, and that he is the one 'Isa son of Maryam gave good news of. Settle wherever you wish. By Allah, were it not for the kingship I am in, I would go to him until I carry his sandals and perform his ablution for him." He ordered the gifts of the other two to be returned to them. Then 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud hastened and reached Badr, and he claimed that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for him when news of his death reached him.[[The Musnad (1/461).]]

This story has been related from Ja'far and Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with them both, and its place is in the books of Sirah (biography). The purpose is that the prophets, peace be upon them, never ceased to describe him and relate him in their books to their nations, and to command them to follow him, support him, and assist him when he is sent. The matter became well known among the people of the earth through the words of Ibrahim the Friend, the father of the prophets after him, when he supplicated for the people of Makkah that Allah send among them a Messenger from themselves; and likewise through the words of 'Isa son of Maryam. For this reason they said: "Tell us about the beginning of your affair," meaning: in the earth. He said: "The supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa son of Maryam, and the vision my mother saw." That is: the trace of that appeared among the people of Makkah, and the premonition of his mention, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

"Ḥaddathana Abu al-Yaman, ḥaddathana Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, from his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser) through whom Allah erases disbelief, I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer) at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am al-‘Aqib (the Last).'"

Muslim also reported it, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with similar wording.[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4896, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2354.]]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Ḥaddathana al-Mas'udi, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named for us some names of himself, some of which we memorized, and he said: "I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, al-Hashir, al-Muqaffi, Prophet of Mercy, of Repentance, and of the Great Battle."

Muslim reported it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with the same.[[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 492, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2355.]] Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Injil﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you shall believe in him and support him. He said: Do you affirm, and accept My covenant on that? They said: We affirm. He said: Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 81]

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah did not send any prophet without taking from him the covenant: "If Muhammad is sent while you are alive, you shall surely follow him," and He took from him that he should take the same covenant from his nation: "If Muhammad is sent while they are alive, they shall surely follow him and support him."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Ḥaddathani Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell us about yourself." He said: "The supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa, and my mother saw when she was carrying me, as if a light came out of her, by which the palaces of Busra in the land of Sham were illuminated."[[Reported by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/600) through Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Ibn Ishaq with it, and he said: "Khalid ibn Ma'dan is among the best of the Successors; he accompanied Mu'adh ibn Jabal and those after him from the Companions. So when a hadith is traced to the Companions, its chain is sound even if they did not include it." I say: It has also been transmitted with a connected chain, as will come in the narration of Ahmad.]]

This is a good chain. It has supporting narrations from other routes. Imam Ahmad said: Ḥaddathana 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, ḥaddathana Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from Sa'id ibn Suwayd al-Kalbi, from 'Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal [in A: "Bilal"] al-Sulami, from al-'Irbad ibn Sariyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I am, with Allah, the Seal of the Prophets, and Adam was still kneaded in his clay. I will inform you of the first of that: the supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa about me, and the vision my mother saw. Likewise, the mothers of the prophets see visions."[[The Musnad (4/127). Sa'id ibn Suwayd was declared reliable only by Ibn Hibban.]]

Ahmad also said: Ḥaddathana Abu al-Nadr, ḥaddathana al-Faraj ibn Fadalah, ḥaddathana Luqman ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard Abu Umamah say: I said: "O Prophet of Allah, what was the beginning of your affair?" He said: "The supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa, and my mother saw that a light came out of her, by which the palaces of Sham were illuminated."[[The Musnad (5/262).]]

Ahmad also said: Ḥaddathana Hasan ibn Musa: I heard Khudayj, the brother of Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiyah, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent us to the Negus, and we were about eighty men, among them 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Ja'far, 'Abdullah ibn [‘Urfutah]  [[Addition from the Musnad; there is a blank in the other manuscripts.]], 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, and Abu Musa. They came to the Negus, and Quraysh sent 'Amr ibn al-'As and 'Umarah ibn al-Walid with a gift. When the two entered upon the Negus, they prostrated to him, then they came at him from his right and his left, and said to him: "Some men from our cousin's people have settled in your land, and they have turned away from us and from our religion." He said: "Where are they?" They said: "They are in your land, so send for them." So he sent for them. Ja'far said: "I will be your speaker today." They followed him. He greeted and did not prostrate. They said to him: "Why do you not prostrate to the king?" He said: "We do not prostrate except to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." He said: "And what is that?" He said: "Indeed Allah sent His Messenger to us, and commanded us not to prostrate to anyone except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and commanded us with prayer and zakat."

'Amr ibn al-'As said: "Indeed they oppose you regarding 'Isa son of Maryam." He said: "What do you say about 'Isa son of Maryam and his mother?" They said: "We say as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: He is the Word of Allah and His Spirit, which He cast to the virgin chaste, whom no man has touched and no child has entered." He took a stick from the ground and said: "O assembly of Abyssinians, priests and monks, by Allah, they do not exceed what we say about him, not even this much. Welcome to you and to those who came from his presence. I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, and that he is the one we find in the Gospel, and that he is the one 'Isa son of Maryam gave good news of. Settle wherever you wish. By Allah, were it not for the kingship I am in, I would go to him until I carry his sandals and perform his ablution for him." He ordered the gifts of the other two to be returned to them. Then 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud hastened and reached Badr, and he claimed that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for him when news of his death reached him.[[The Musnad (1/461).]]

This story has been related from Ja'far and Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with them both, and its place is in the books of Sirah (biography). The purpose is that the prophets, peace be upon them, never ceased to describe him and relate him in their books to their nations, and to command them to follow him, support him, and assist him when he is sent. The matter became well known among the people of the earth through the words of Ibrahim the Friend, the father of the prophets after him, when he supplicated for the people of Makkah that Allah send among them a Messenger from themselves; and likewise through the words of 'Isa son of Maryam. For this reason they said: "Tell us about the beginning of your affair," meaning: in the earth. He said: "The supplication of my father Ibrahim, the good news of 'Isa son of Maryam, and the vision my mother saw." That is: the trace of that appeared among the people of Makkah, and the premonition of his mention, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 61, verses 10–13:

It has already been mentioned in the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Salam that the Companions (ṣaḥābah, may Allah be pleased with them) wished to ask about the deeds most beloved to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so that they might perform them. Then Allah revealed this surah, and among its contents is this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment?﴾ Then He explained this great transaction, which never perishes, and which achieves the desired aim and removes the feared harm, saying: ﴿You believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive in the way of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew.﴾ That is, better than the trade of this world, and than toiling for it and devoting oneself to it alone.

Then He said: ﴿He will forgive you your sins﴾ That is: if you do what I have commanded you and guided you to, I will forgive you your lapses, cause you to enter Gardens, pure dwellings, and lofty levels. For this reason He said: ﴿and admit you to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, and pleasant dwellings in Gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great triumph.﴾

Then He said: ﴿And another [favour] that you love﴾ That is: and I will add to that an addition you love, which is: ﴿help from Allah and an imminent victory.﴾ That is: if you fight in His way and support His religion, Allah will take upon Himself your victory. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm﴾ [Muhammad: 7], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah will surely support whoever supports Him. Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty﴾ [Al-Hajj: 40]. As for His saying ﴿and an imminent victory﴾, that means swift. So this addition is the good of this world joined to the bliss of the Hereafter, for those who obey Allah and His Messenger and support Allah and His religion. For this reason He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers.﴾

Allah the Exalted says, commanding His believing servants to be helpers of Allah in all their circumstances, with their words, their deeds, their selves and their wealth, and to respond to Allah and His Messenger, just as the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) responded to 'Isa when he said: ﴿Who are my helpers in reaching Allah?﴾ That is, who will assist me in calling to Allah, Mighty and Majestic? ﴿The disciples said⁠—they were the followers of 'Isa, peace be upon him⁠—﴾: ﴿We are the helpers of Allah.﴾ That is, we are your helpers in what you have been sent with, and we will support you in it. For this reason he sent them as callers to the people in the lands of al-Sham, among the Israelites and the Greeks.

And this is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say during the days of Hajj: "Is there a man who will give me shelter until I convey the message of my Lord, for the Quraysh have prevented me from conveying the message of my Lord?" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (3/322) from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prepared for him al-Aws and al-Khazraj from the people of Madinah, and they pledged allegiance to him, supported him, and stipulated that they would protect him from black and red alike if he migrated to them. When he migrated to them with those of his companions who were with him, they fulfilled to him what they had pledged to Allah. For this reason Allah and His Messenger named them al-Ansar (the Helpers), and this became their distinguishing title, may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased.

As for His saying: ﴿So a group of the Children of Israel believed, and a group disbelieved﴾: that is, when 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, conveyed the message of his Lord to his people, and those who supported him among the disciples supported him, a group of the Children of Israel was guided by what he brought them, while another group went astray, departed from what he had brought them, denied his prophethood, and accused him and his mother of great evils. These were the Jews, upon whom be the successive curses of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Another group among his followers exceeded the limits concerning him, until they raised him above what Allah had given him of prophethood. They split into sects and factions. Among them is one who says: "He is the son of Allah." Another says: "He is the third of three: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit." Another says: "He is Allah." All of these statements are explained in detail in Surat an-Nisa'.

As for His saying: ﴿So We supported those who believed against their enemy﴾: that is, We gave them victory over those among the Christian sects who opposed them. ﴿So they became dominant﴾: that is, over them. This was by the sending of Muhammad ﷺ, as Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said.

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal (meaning Ibn 'Amr), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended to raise 'Isa up to the heavens, he went out to his companions, who were in a house, twelve men, from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping water. He said: "Among you is one who will disbelieve in me twelve times after he has believed in me." He said: Then he said: "Which of you will be made to look like me, and be killed in my place, and be with me in my rank?" He said: A young man from the youngest of them stood up and said: "I." He said to him: "Sit down." Then he repeated it to them, and the young man stood up and said: "I." He said to him: "Sit down." Then he repeated it again, and the young man stood up and said: "I." He said: "Yes, you are that one." He said: So the likeness of 'Isa was cast upon him, and 'Isa, peace be upon him, was raised up from an opening in the house to the heavens. He said: The Jews came in pursuit, and they seized his likeness, killed him, and crucified him. And some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after having believed in him, and they split into three sects concerning him. One sect said: "Allah was among us as long as He willed, then He ascended to the heavens." These are the Ya'qubiyyah. Another sect said: "The son of Allah was among us as long as Allah willed, then He raised him to Himself." These are the Nestorians. And another sect said: "The servant of Allah and His Messenger was among us as long as Allah willed, then He raised him to Himself." These are the Muslims. Then the two disbelieving sects united against the Muslim sect, and they killed it. Islam remained obscured until Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿So a group of the Children of Israel believed, and a group disbelieved﴾: meaning the group among the Children of Israel that disbelieved in the time of 'Isa, and the group that believed in the time of 'Isa. ﴿So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant﴾ by the manifestation of Muhammad ﷺ's religion over the religion of the disbelievers. ﴿And they became dominant.﴾

This is his wording in his book in explaining this noble verse. Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it in explaining this verse in his Sunan, from Abu Kurayb, from Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', from Abu Mu'awiyah, with the same wording. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/60) and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11591).]]

Thus the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ will continue to be dominant upon the truth, until the command of Allah comes while they are still in that state, and until the last of them fights the Dajjal alongside the Messiah 'Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, as the authentic hadiths have related [[Addition from manuscripts M and A.]]. And Allah knows best.
